title: Regional capacity scout brief — week of 2026-05-02
content:
Purpose:
This is the weekly "scout" brief from the regional capacity working group for infra leads and SRE. The scout synthesizes observed signals, near-term requests, and recommended allocation moves for GPU fleets across regions (US-W, US-E, EU, AP-SE, AP-North). The goal is to give product and platform teams a short, operational picture and specific action items to avoid late-afternoon throttles and to prepare for the upcoming demo week (2026-05-10 -> 2026-05-14).

Summary highlights (top-of-page):
- Overall utilization: 72% fleet-wide (up 6% week-over-week).
- Hotspots: US-W burst corridor (p95 latency spikes during 14:00–17:00 PDT) and AP-SE preemption surges tied to spot provider maintenance windows.
- Immediate ask: shift 12 RTX-A6000 equivalent units from EU reserve to US-W for next 7 days to cover sustained increase in streaming workloads (proposal in linked PR).
- Risk: soft-eviction threshold currently 85% in US-W; if we cross 88% for >4 hours we will trigger automated spillover (evict noncritical Dedicated jobs).

Observable signals and notes:
- Latency and queue signals
  - US-W 95th token latency increased from 42ms to 98ms during busy window; tracing shows longer KV cache misses on serving nodes provisioning new contexts.
  - Queue build-up correlated with new internal loadgen from product team (demo harness INF-3421).

- Allocation and capacity changes
  - EU pool: compact-allocation rollout completed on 2026-04-30; immediate effect: -9% per-token cost for embeddings workloads but reduced headroom for large-chat instances.
  - AP-SE: two preemptible racks scheduled maintenance on 2026-05-04; current plan re-routes burst to AP-North and US-E.
  - US-E: low utilization overnight — candidate region to absorb AP-SE burst if we can extend cross-region auto-routing windows (see action 2).

- Prewarming + KV cache behavior
  - Experiment: prefix prewarm script reduced cold-start tail by ~30% for conversational traces in US-W (A/B test run from 2026-04-28 to 2026-05-01).
  - Observed regression for long-context models when prewarm concurrency > 8 (memory pressure). Need fail-safe to drop to cold path if swap increases.

- Incidents and postmortem notes
  - 2026-05-01 15:40 PDT — partial latency degradation in US-W. Short blip resolved by scaling policy ramp; root cause: concurrent staging traffic from solutions-eng plus a delayed autoscaler evaluation cycle (race with spot eviction). Ticket INF-3498 created.

Recommendations (operational):
1) Short-term (0–72h):
   - Approve a temporary transfer of 12 A6000-equivalent units from EU reserve to US-W (elastic reserved mapping). Rationale: avoids hitting soft-eviction threshold during demo week. Owner: Marco. Target completion: 2026-05-04 09:00 PDT.
   - Disable compact-allocation backfill for chat-large class in EU until 2026-05-07 to preserve headroom for rollbacks. Owner: Elena.

2) Medium-term (3–14d):
   - Extend cross-region auto-routing time window for AP-SE->US-E fallback (02:00–20:00 UTC) and test with canary traffic. Action: infra-routing team to create canary route and observe cost delta. Owner: Samir. Jira: INF-3512.
   - Harden prewarm fail-safe: implement memory probe that drops concurrency if RSS > threshold; include telemetry tag to filter prewarm-caused tail spikes. Owner: Aisha. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1829

3) Policy and capacity-planning:
   - Re-evaluate soft-eviction thresholds by region; recommend lowering US-W to 83% for next 30 days while demo week is active to avoid user-facing spillovers. Discussion in next capacity sync.
   - Prepare a standby pool of 16 preemptible nodes in US-W tagged "demo-standby" that can be quickly converted to non-preemptible for 72h in emergencies. Cost acceptance signed off by finance (email thread).

Open questions and blockers:
- Approval flow for intra-reserve reassignments: can infra move EU reserve to US-W without sales/finance sign-off for up to 7 days? Need clarity — flagged to infra-ops and finance.
- Cross-region bandwidth egress estimates: shifting sustained traffic to US-W from EU may increase egress by ~2.5TB/day; product-team sign-off required.

Action list (owners and due dates):
- Marco Chen: execute 12-unit transfer EU->US-W; due 2026-05-04.
- Elena Rodriguez: pause compact-backfill for chat-large in EU; due 2026-05-04.
- Samir Gupta: create routing canary and run 24h smoke; due 2026-05-06.
- Aisha Patel: land prewarm memory-probe and add telemetry tag; PR link above; due 2026-05-05.
- Oncall rotation note: Tom L. will cover infra oncall 2026-05-03 -> 2026-05-05; escalate to SRE lead if soft-eviction triggers.

Meeting cadence and next checkpoints:
- Ad-hoc capacity huddle if US-W crosses 85% for >2h.
- Weekly capacity review scheduled 2026-05-06 09:00 PDT (calendar invite: #infra-capacity-weekly).

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Fleet utilization (fleet-wide): 72%
- US-W: 88% peak in busy corridor, 72% average
- EU: 60% avg, compact rollout effect visible
- AP-SE: 67% avg, two racks scheduled maintenance 2026-05-04
- Standby preemptible pool size: 40 nodes total (16 recommended to preassign for demo standby)

Notes to reviewers:
- This brief is intentionally concise. For the full dataset, charts, and per-application token-level traces see the Capacity Scout Confluence page (linked above) and the PR for the automated transfer. Please call out any downstream product impacts (especially egress/cost) in replies so we can include in the finance approval thread.

End of scout brief.
